S002.name: Sustained_Attention_Difficulty
S002.description: Often has difficulty sustaining attention in tasks or play activities.
examples: Focuses at first during class or meetings but soon becomes distracted or spaces out.
Re-reads the same paragraph in a book multiple times but the content does not register.
Loses focus while watching movies or TV and misses the plot.
Unable to maintain attention until the end of a long meeting or lecture, often drifting off or becoming drowsy.

S003.name: Listening_Difficulty
S003.description: Often does not seem to listen when spoken to directly.
examples: Appears not to be listening, looking elsewhere or spacing out during conversation.
Immediately asks to repeat what was just said or instructed.
Does not respond when name is called or answers only after a long delay.
Misses the content of the conversation, giving unrelated answers or out-of-context reactions.

S004.name: Instruction_Follow through_Difficulty
S004.description: Often does not follow through on instructions and fails to finish schoolwork, chores, or duties in the workplace.
examples: Starts homework or projects but fails to complete them, submitting unfinished work or missing deadlines.
When given multi-step instructions, follows only the first few steps and forgets the rest.
Starts cleaning or organizing but switches to another task midway, failing to finish.
Leaves almost completed work reports or paperwork unfinished, neglecting the final steps.

S007.name: Losing_Items
S007.description: Often loses things necessary for tasks or activities.
examples: Frequently loses school supplies or office supplies like pens, erasers, and calculators.
Always searching for glasses, cell phones, wallets, or keys because they do not know where they are.
Loses necessary documents or materials at home or in the office and cannot find them.
Cannot remember where they placed an item they were holding just moments ago.

S009.name: Daily_Activities_Forgetfulness
S009.description: Often forgetful in daily activities (e.g., doing chores, running errands; for older adolescents and adults, returning calls, paying bills, keeping appointments).
examples: Forgets appointment times or meeting schedules, arriving late or missing them entirely.
Forgets to reply to received calls or messages for days.
Frequently incurs late fees because of missing deadlines for utility bills or credit card payments.
Forgets to take medication or leaves necessary items at home when going out.

symptom.disease_info: Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder, Predominantly Inattentive Presentation is a neurodevelopmental condition marked by persistent inattention that interferes with functioning across settings, often becoming more clinically visible when life demands exceed the person’s compensatory routines. Typical presentation includes difficulty sustaining attention, seeming not to listen, poor follow-through, losing necessary items, and forgetfulness, without prominent hyperactive-impulsive symptoms. It is distinguished from situational stress, depression, anxiety, or cognitive decline by its persistent attentional pattern, developmental course, and functional impairment not better explained by another condition.

patient.stressor: Amanda’s facilities department underwent a major readjustment when a new management company introduced digital work orders, energy-efficiency audits, and tighter documentation standards tied to her hoped-for promotion into senior facilities management. Across the following 11 months, her long-standing reliance on handwritten checklists and physical routines was no longer enough: she had trouble sustaining attention during multi-step service requests, lost tools and tablets needed for jobs, forgot scheduled callbacks, and left several maintenance duties unfinished despite understanding the instructions. The resulting backlog, complaints from building occupants, and a formal safety review after a near-miss made the impairment impossible to dismiss as ordinary workplace pressure. She entered psychiatric care through an occupational health referral after choosing to pursue evaluation rather than abandon the promotion track she had worked toward for years.

S002.name: Sustained_Attention_Difficulty
S002.description: Often has difficulty sustaining attention in tasks or play activities.
S002.manifestation: I can start a digital work order thinking I’ve got it, but halfway through reading the notes my mind slips off to the next noise or job and I realize I don’t know what I just looked at.

S003.name: Listening_Difficulty
S003.description: Often does not seem to listen when spoken to directly.
S003.manifestation: When my supervisor talks straight to me about a repair or audit, I’ll be looking right at him, but only the first part sticks and then I have to ask him to say it again.

S004.name: Instruction_Follow through_Difficulty
S004.description: Often does not follow through on instructions and fails to finish schoolwork, chores, or duties in the workplace.
S004.manifestation: I’ll begin a maintenance job, do the actual fix, and then somehow leave the last steps like closing the ticket, labeling the panel, or checking back with the tenant undone.

S007.name: Losing_Items
S007.description: Often loses things necessary for tasks or activities.
S007.manifestation: I’m constantly hunting for the tablet, keys, flashlight, or the one tool I had in my hand a minute ago, and it’s gotten bad enough that it holds up jobs and makes me look careless.

S009.name: Daily_Activities_Forgetfulness
S009.description: Often forgetful in daily activities (e.g., doing chores, running errands; for older adolescents and adults, returning calls, paying bills, keeping appointments).
S009.manifestation: What brought me in is I keep forgetting scheduled callbacks, work orders, and even basic follow-ups I promised people, and now it’s piled up so much that work sent me here before I lose my shot at moving up.

add_requirements.Onset prior to age 12 years: I remember being this way back in grade school, long before any of this job pressure—teachers said I was bright but always misplaced papers, missed parts of directions, and needed reminders to finish classwork.
add_requirements.functional_impairment: The problems have turned into a serious work issue now: I have a backlog, tenant complaints, and a safety review on my record, and I’m scared it may cost me the promotion path I’ve been working toward.
add_requirements.duration: It’s been noticeably worse for about 11 months, since the new management company changed our department over to digital work orders and stricter documentation.
